page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-90-lssd is a server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 90 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 45 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 360.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled directly, consisting of 3216 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity distributed across 8 local SSDs. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU capabilities, with the stress-ng multi-core test and PassMark CPU score ranking in the top 10%. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, and BF16) and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI, which contribute to top-tier performance in PassMark extended instructions and encryption tests. Software compilation with Clang and ray tracing benchmarks also achieve top-tier results. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded compression tests falling into the average range.

The memory subsystem delivers strong read bandwidth, reaching 6372.53 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 217.44 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Large block write bandwidth is average at 76.89 GB/sec. Database operations perform strongly, with PassMark database operations in the top 25% and Redis SET operations reaching a top-tier throughput of 117.73 million operations per second. Large-scale prompt processing for small LLM models also registers in the top 10%, though text generation speeds for larger models scale down to average tiers.

The instance offers high resource density for compute and local storage, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require high-speed local scratch space and massive parallel processing without the overhead of external network storage. The primary tradeoff is the lack of GPU acceleration and the moderate single-threaded performance relative to its multi-core capacity. This hardware profile is suited for high-throughput database deployments, software compilation pipelines, Redis caching layers, and parallelized CPU-bound simulations.
